A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of multiproton magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for the diagnosis and staging of prostate cancer (PC) has increased significantly over the past 10 years.
MRI can help to identify patients who can safely avoid biopsy and also to guide biopsy to the area that is most likely to harbor cancer.
mpMRI has an important role in the evaluation of localized PCa and is emerging as a key component in the management of men on active surveillance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mpMRI is an important tool to guide AS, but it should not be used to replace a clinical decision to pursue active surveillance in a patient with favorable disease.
there is a need for prospective validation and standardization of the role of mpMRI for PCa.
